Every clique stays complete and is joined to the next one around the ring by a single plain edge." width="100%"} Creates `num_cliques` complete graphs of `clique_size` nodes and adds one edge from each clique to the next, closing the ring with an edge from the last clique back to the first. Unlike the connected caveman graph (see `add_connected_caveman_graph()`), the cliques stay complete, so the graph has `num_cliques * clique_size(clique_size - 1)/2 + num_cliques` edges. The construction matches NetworkX's `ring_of_cliques()`: the second node of each clique is joined to the first node of the next. Each node's clique (`0`, `1`, ...) is stored in the `community_attr=` node attribute. The cliques are created in ring order, each as a consecutive run of node IDs. In a directed graph every edge inside a clique points from the earlier-created node to the later one, and the ring edges run forward from each clique to the next. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Rings of cliques are useful for: - showing the resolution limit of modularity: with many small cliques, merging neighboring cliques scores higher than keeping them apart, although each clique is clearly its own community - test cases for community detection with a known, unambiguous answer - modeling teams that each keep one contact with the next team along a chain of command or supply ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [num_cliques]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of cliques on the ring. Must be at least `2`. [clique_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in each clique. Must be at least `2`. [community_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["community"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's clique index. Default is `"community"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `num_cliques=` or `clique_size=` is less than `2`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Six triangles in a ring give `18` nodes and `6 * 3 + 6 = 24` edges: ::: {#9798d826 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_ring_of_cliques(num_cliques=6, clique_size=3) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (18, 24) ``` ::: ::: With 30 triangles, pairing up neighboring triangles gives a higher modularity than the planted partition into single triangles, an example of the resolution limit: ::: {#e7e173bb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ring = ec.Graph().add_ring_of_cliques(num_cliques=30, clique_size=3) pairs = {nid: c // 2 for nid, c in ring.get_node_attrs("community").items()} round(ring.modularity("community"), 3), round(ring.modularity(pairs), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (0.717, 0.808) ``` ::: :::
